label: <DEL> step of long sequences that start with y
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (99.9% of mass), i.e. when the model is about to output original token 0. About 87% of mass comes from sequences whose first token is y (lift 24x); most of the rest is first token 0, e, or g. It needs long sequences: L=7-9 only (52% of mass at L=8), nothing for L<=5. The predicate catches ~81% of activations and ~87% of mass, but precision is low (~8%): most long y-initial sequences do not fire it, so it is a sparse subset of this context. Presence of k/o/w/z among the original tokens raises the firing rate somewhat (~1.7x) but does not cleanly separate active from inactive cases. Magnitude is higher for top examples (y-initial, L=8-9). It does not fire in the original or copy phases.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=3 (+3.05), phase=1 & out_tok=0 (+3.03), orig2=k (+2.81), phase=1 & out_tok=y (+2.62), orig3=k (+2.30), prev_tok=2 (+2.20). Lower it: orig6=- (-4.24), in_first=0 (-4.15), orig1=3 (-2.20), in_count=1 (-1.99).
